grammarPoints.title: Comparing two choices
grammarPoints.meaning: Say which of two things has more of a quality, or ask which one does.
grammarPoints.formation: A のほうが B より adjective です. Question: A と B と、どちらのほうが adjective ですか.
notes: のほうが identifies the higher side and より the comparison standard; word order may change without reversing the meaning.
The adjective itself does not get a special comparative ending. どっち is a more conversational alternative to どちら.

grammarPoints.title: Choosing the most from a group
grammarPoints.meaning: Identify the highest degree of a quality among three or more choices.
grammarPoints.formation: Group の中で、item がいちばん adjective です. Ask with the suitable question word + がいちばん.
notes: Use どれ for a visible list of items, 何 for many category questions, だれ for people, どこ for places, and いつ for times.
For three or more choices, do not replace the superlative pattern with どっち or のほう.

grammarPoints.title: Replacing a known noun with の
grammarPoints.meaning: Avoid repeating a thing already identified: “the small one,” “the clean one,” or “Aki’s.”
grammarPoints.formation: I-adjective + の; na-adjective + な + の; possessor noun + の.
notes: The missing noun must be recoverable from context. In ordinary descriptions of people, use 人 rather than this “one” pattern.
Possessive の appears just once: あきさんの, not あきさんのの.

grammarPoints.title: Intentions with つもり
grammarPoints.meaning: Describe an intention to do or avoid an action. A past form describes an earlier plan.
grammarPoints.formation: Nonpast short verb + つもりです; nonpast negative + つもりです. Earlier plan: verb + つもりでした.
notes: Keep the action verb nonpast even when the intention is past.
A plan is stronger than simply wondering about an action. Use a controllable action and a person who can intend it.

grammarPoints.title: Becoming different: なる
grammarPoints.meaning: Describe a change of state, degree, or role.
grammarPoints.formation: I-adjective: remove い and add くなる. Na-adjective or noun: add になる. Conjugate なる for time and politeness.
notes: Do not say 大きいになる. いい becomes よくなる.
A change can be absolute or relative. 前より explicitly compares with before.

grammarPoints.title: Somewhere, someone, and their negatives
grammarPoints.meaning: Refer to an unspecified place or person, or say that none was involved.
grammarPoints.formation: どこかに / だれかに with an affirmative or question; どこにも / だれにも with a negative predicate.
notes: Particles such as に, へ, and で follow か but come before negative も: どこかで / どこでも + negative.
In these basic patterns, 何か and 何も do not need を. Negative も requires a negative predicate.

grammarPoints.title: Means, tools, and language with で
grammarPoints.meaning: Name the means of transport, tool, medium, or language used to do something.
grammarPoints.formation: Means noun + で + action. The destination still takes に or へ; an object still takes を.
notes: A location can also take で, but here で answers “by what means?”
“On foot” is 歩いて, not a transport noun plus で. Match tools to actions they can perform.

grammarPoints.title: Extra: do something and come back
grammarPoints.meaning: Use てくる when an action happens elsewhere and is followed by movement toward the current location.
grammarPoints.formation: Verb te-form + 来る; polite nonpast 〜てきます, past 〜てきました.
notes: Context must establish a return or movement toward the speaker’s reference location.
This introductory use is physical movement; do not generate later abstract “has begun to” meanings.

grammarPoints.title: Extra: leaving room for a reply with が or けど
grammarPoints.meaning: End with が or けど to offer relevant information and invite the other person to respond.
grammarPoints.formation: Polite sentence + が…; conversational sentence + けど….
notes: The unfinished ending can soften a request or let the listener choose. It need not mean a strong contradiction.
Provide a conversational opening in the scenario so that the incomplete ending has a purpose.
